A DHT11 or DHT22 (AM2302) temperature and humidity sensor on one data pin: Read gives both — with how hot it feels and the dew point — and Climate Trigger runs a branch when one of them goes past a limit.

actions.description: The temperature and the humidity — with how hot it feels (heat index) and the dew point. Fallback when the sensor doesn't answer, with the reason in error.

configurations.description: Board pin wired to the sensor's data (DATA / S / OUT). A bare sensor needs a 10 kΩ pull-up from it to 3.3 V; a module has one.
Which sensor it is — DHT11 (blue, 0-50 °C, 1 reading a second) or DHT22 / AM2302 (white, -40-80 °C, finer, 1 every 2 s).
What temperature, heat_index and dew_point are in.

outputSchema.name: temperature
outputSchema.description: The temperature, in Unit — a DHT11 reads it in whole degrees.

outputSchema.name: humidity
outputSchema.description: The relative humidity, 0 to 100 %.

outputSchema.name: heat_index
outputSchema.description: How hot it feels, in Unit — the temperature itself in cool air, higher when it's hot and humid.

outputSchema.name: dew_point
outputSchema.description: The temperature the air would fog (and surfaces sweat) at, in Unit.

outputSchema.name: error
outputSchema.description: Why it's Fallback — no_pin, no_answer (the wiring, the pull-up, the Model picked or its power); empty otherwise.

triggers.description: Runs its branch when the temperature or the humidity goes above (or below) Limit — read every Interval. It fires again only once the value came back past Hysteresis, so one sitting right on Limit doesn't fire over and over. Past Limit when the program starts counts as getting there.

A monochrome I2C OLED — SSD1306 (0.96", 128x64 or 128x32) or SH1106 (1.3", 128x64), 4 pins. Print text in 3 fonts and 4 sizes, Scroll it, Draw shapes (any shape from its vertices), show an Image (built-in icons or your own bitmap), and readings as a Bar, a Gauge or a Chart over time. Actions draw into a buffer and Update Screen sends it — turn it off on all but the last to build a screen without flicker.

actions.description: Writes text — or a bound value, like a sensor's reading — on a line of the screen, in one of 4 sizes.

configurations.description: Board pin wired to the display's SDA.
Board pin wired to the display's SCL (sometimes labeled SCK).
The display's controller and size — 0.96" modules are usually SSD1306, 1.3" ones SH1106 (picking SSD1306 for one shows a shifted, noisy image).
What to show — type it, or bind an output or a variable (numbers are formatted, see Decimals). A typed \n goes on to the next line. Accents show as their plain letter.
Which line to write on, from 1 at the top — lines are 8 px: 1 to 8 on a 64-px screen, 1 to 4 on a 32-px one. A bigger Text Size takes more lines from there down.
The typeface — Standard (8 px a character, 16 a line), Small (a finer 5x7, 6 px a character: 21 a line, with descenders) or Bold (Standard 1 px thicker, 9 px a character: 14 a line).
How big the text is — 1x to 4x the font (8, 16, 24 or 32 px tall), taking that many 8-px lines from Line down.
Where on the line the text goes.
Which character the text starts at, from 1 — up to 16 in Standard at 1x, 21 in Small (fewer at bigger sizes).
Text around Text — {} stands for it: "Temp: {} C". Without {}, it goes before it.
Decimal places of a bound number that isn't whole, from 0 to 6.
Blank the line (all of its height) before writing, so a shorter text doesn't leave the end of the last one behind.

A PWM signal on a pin — for dimming a LED, setting a DC motor's speed (through a driver or transistor), driving a buzzer. Write sets a duty and holds it, Fade moves to one smoothly over a time, Stop cuts the signal. For servos, use the Servo component.

actions.description: Puts a PWM signal on the pin — Duty % of the time on — and holds it until the next action on the pin.

configurations.description: Board pin the signal goes out on — only PWM-capable pins are listed.
How much of the time the pin is on, from 0 (off) to 100 (fully on), in %. Decimals are fine (12.5). Bind it to follow a sensor.
Signal frequency, from 1 to 40000 Hz. 1000 suits LEDs; motors run quieter at 20000 (out of hearing); on a buzzer it's the note.
How Duty maps to the signal. Perceived brightness follows how the eye sees light, so a LED dims evenly (50% looks half as bright); keep Linear for motors and buzzers.
On for a load that's on when the pin is LOW — a LED wired from 3.3 V to the pin, an active-low driver. 100% is then fully on.
configurations.label: Active low

outputSchema.name: duty
outputSchema.description: The duty set, in % (0–100).

outputSchema.name: frequency
outputSchema.description: The frequency set, in Hz.

actions.description: Moves the pin's duty smoothly to To over Duration, then holds it — a LED fading in or out, a motor easing up.

On for a load that's on when the pin is LOW — a LED wired from 3.3 V to the pin, an active-low driver. 100% is then fully on.
